1.w: Better is a poor person who walks in his integrity than one who is perverse in his speech and is a fool.

2.w: It is dangerous to have zeal without knowledge, and the one who acts hastily makes poor choices.

3.w: A person’s folly subverts his way, and his heart rages against the Lord.

4.w: Wealth adds many friends, but a poor person is separated from his friend.

5.w: A false witness will not go unpunished, and the one who spouts out lies will not escape punishment.

6.w: Many people entreat the favor of a generous person, and everyone is the friend of the person who gives gifts.

7.w: All the relatives of a poor person hate him; how much more do his friends avoid him— one who chases words, which are nothing.

8.w: The one who acquires understanding loves himself; the one who preserves understanding will prosper.

9.w: A false witness will not go unpunished, and the one who spouts out lies will perish.

10.w: Luxury is not appropriate for a fool; how much less for a servant to rule over princes!

11.w: A person’s wisdom has made him slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.

12.w: A king’s wrath is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.

13.w: A foolish child is the ruin of his father, and a contentious wife is like a constant dripping.

14.w: A house and wealth are inherited from parents, but a prudent wife is from the Lord.

15.w: Laziness brings on a deep sleep, and the idle person will go hungry.

16.w: The one who obeys commandments guards his life; the one who despises his ways will die.

17.w: The one who is gracious to the poor lends to the Lord, and the Lord will repay him for his good deed.

18.w: Discipline your child, for there is hope, but do not set your heart on causing his death.

19.w: A person with great anger bears the penalty, but if you deliver him from it once, you will have to do it again.

20.w: Listen to advice and receive discipline, that you may become wise by the end of your life.

21.w: There are many plans in a person’s mind, but it is the counsel of the Lord that will stand.

22.w: What is desirable for a person is to show loyal love, and a poor person is better than a liar.

23.w: Fearing the Lord leads to life, and one who does so will live satisfied; he will not be afflicted by calamity.

24.w: The sluggard has plunged his hand into the dish, and he will not even bring it back to his mouth!

25.w: Flog a scorner, and as a result the simpleton will learn prudence; correct a discerning person, and as a result he will understand knowledge.

26.w: The one who robs his father and chases away his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.

27.w: If you stop listening to instruction, my child, you will stray from the words of knowledge.

28.w: A crooked witness scorns justice, and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity.

29.w: Penalties have been prepared for scorners, and floggings for the backs of fools.
